previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and major depression was admitted due to altered mental status and difficulty standing, as noticed by her daughter. The confusion was multifactorial, stemming from noncompliance with lactulose, recent alcohol use, and accidental overdose of psychiatric medications, particularly taking double doses of Wellbutrin and excess Seroquel. She was treated with lactulose, vitamin supplementation, and benzodiazepines for alcohol withdrawal symptoms, while all sedating and anticholinergic medications were held. Her mental status improved over several days, and she was restarted on a simplified regimen of bupropion and trazodone per psychiatry. Labs showed stable thrombocytopenia and leukopenia, and imaging revealed cirrhotic changes without acute findings. She was discharged home with services, new supplements for alcohol-related deficiencies, and plans for outpatient follow-up in psychiatry, hepatology, and a geriatric day program for ongoing support.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ female with a history of HCV/EtOH 
cirrhosis (decompensated by HE, varices (grade 1 varices x 2 on 
EGD ___, who presents with abdominal pain and CTA abdomen 
showing colitis.  MELD 14, DF 29. 

ACUTE ISSUES
============
# Abdominal Pain: Patient presented with right upper quadrant 
abdominal pain.  CTA abdomen did not show any obstruction or 
mesenteric ischemia. Concern for infectious colitis given 
location in R colon, nausea and vomiting however she denied any 
diarrhea. Initially started on ciprofloxacin and flagyl however 
these were discontinued.  Her  abdominal ultrasound does not 
show any ascites, biliary obstruction, or hepatic clots. No 
signs of acute abdomen on physical exam. Alcoholic hepatitis was 
possible given elevated AST>ALT and elevated bilirubin compared 
to prior admission. Her discriminate function 29 as of ___. 
Patient reports drinking recently as of ___. However no 
other signs of alcoholic hepatitis. Steroids were not needed 
given her discriminate function. The patient also has a history 
of marijuana use and cyclical vomiting syndrome was also on the 
differential. No antibiotics were given. The patient started to 
have nausea, vomiting and loose stools during her hospital stay. 
Stool cultures were sent. The patient underwent flex 
sigmoidoscopy   for concern of guaiac positive stool with 
history of hemorrhoids and polyps. However there was no evidence 
of colitis on the sigmoidoscopy. Her pain improved during the 
hospital stay with morphine and nausea controlled with zofran. 
She went a full infectious work up that showed no other cause. 
She started to tolerate PO well. It is likely that she was 
likely suffering from gastroenteritis. 

# Somnolence: Patient was found to be somnolent on admission to 
the floor. This was likely a combination to the IV morphine and 
her acute illness. She was responsive when woken up and did 
answer questions. Her pain medications were held and continued 
on home lactulose and rifaximin. Her mental status improved 
during her hospital stay and was back to baseline on discharge. 

# Sinus tachycardia: Patient was tachycardic into the 100s on 
admission and continued to remain tachycardic during her 
hospital stay. It was likely secondary to dehydration in setting 
of several episodes of vomiting and no oral intake. Patient has 
no other signs of alcohol withdrawal at this point. However she 
was started on a CIWA protocol which she scored for and then 
resolved prior to discharge.  Her pain was well controlled 
throughout the hospital stay. 
 
# History  of alcohol abuse: patient states her last alcoholic 
beverage was on ___. See above for CIWA. She was 
continued on  folate, thiamine, multivitamin and given ativan 
PRN withdrawal symptoms.  

# Alcoholic/HCV cirrhosis: complicated by ascites, 
encephalopathy (multiple admissions this year for confusion), 2 
grade 1 varices on EGD ___ and portal hypertensive 
gastropathy. HCV genotype 1, reports last drink to be ___. MELD 
16 on admission which is stable from prior admission. Last 
colonoscopy ___ with adenomatous polyps on biopsy, no 
stigmata of bleeding, otherwise normal.  However patient had 
guiac positive stool in setting of polyps so she underwent a 
sigmoidoscopy which showed hemorrhoids. She was continued on 
lactulose and rifaxamin. Her spironolactone was held due to 
hypovolemia during hospital stay and restarted prior to 
discharge. 
 
CHRONIC ISSUES
==============
#Thrombocytopenia: At baseline. Likely related to liver disease 
and alcohol use. No overt signs/symptoms of bleeding at this 
time.  

# Leukopenia: has chronic leukopenia from bone marrow 
suppression from alcohol abuse, WBC on this admission lower than 
previous which may be secondary to infectious process or thought 
to be dilutional .  

# Type 2 diabetes: not on home insulin, started on sliding 
scale, not discharged on insulin. 

# Depression: continued on home medications as per PACT team 
recs

TRANSLATIONAL ISSUES:
- follow up CBC as patient had pancytopenia that was likely 
dilutional

EXAMINATION:  Liver Doppler ultrasound

INDICATION:  Cirrhosis. Abdominal pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Sonographic gray scale and color Doppler images were obtained of
the abdomen.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal/pelvic CT from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The liver shows increased and coarsened echogenicity, consistent with known
cirrhosis. The gallbladder has been surgically removed. The CBD measures up to
10 mm. Visualized portions of the pancreas, including head and body, are
within normal limits.  The spleen measures 11.9 cm and has homogenous
echotexture. Representative image of the right kidney is normal. There is no
ascites.

DOPPLER COLOR FLOW AND SPECTRAL WAVEFORM ANALYSIS: The main, left and right
portal veins are patent with appropriate directionality of flow. However, note
is made of slow flow within the left portal vein. The main hepatic artery
presents a normal waveform.  Limited evaluation of the left hepatic vein.  The
right and middle  hepatic veins are patent. The IVC is within normal limits.
The SMV is patent with appropriate directionality of flow.  Note is made of a
patent recanalized umbilical vein.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Cirrhotic liver.

2. Patent portal veins and hepatic artery with appropriate directionality of
flow and waveforms.  However, note is made of slow flow within the left portal
vein.  Limited examination of the left hepatic vein.  Right and middle hepatic
veins are patent.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT through the abdomen pelvis performed without
using low-dose with an with IV contrast. Arterial phase imaging through the
abdomen pelvis was performed per mesenteric CTA protocol. Multiplanar
reformations provided. No oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:  DLP: ___.20 mGy-cm (abdomen and pelvis.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis from ___ and Doppler ultrasound of
the abdomen performed today.

FINDINGS: 

LUNG BASES:  Areas of subsegmental atelectasis are noted at the lung bases.
The imaged portion of the heart is unremarkable. No worrisome nodule, mass, or
consolidation is seen at the imaged portions of the lower lungs.

CTA:  The abdominal aorta enhances normally with widely patent major branches.
There is no aneurysm or dissection. Mild to moderate atherosclerotic
calcification is seen along the abdominal aorta extending into the iliac
branches.

ABDOMEN: Nodular shrunken liver is compatible with cirrhosis. A recannulized
umbilical vein is noted. The main portal vein appears patent. No discrete
focal liver lesion is identified. The spleen is not enlarged. The gallbladder
is not seen. The adrenal glands are normal. The pancreas appears unremarkable.
The kidneys enhance symmetrically and there are several small hypodensities
within the cortex of the kidneys which are too small to characterize though
likely represent simple cysts. There is no retroperitoneal hematoma or
lymphadenopathy.

There may be mild gastric wall edema with hyperemia of the mucosa. Please
correlate clinically. The duodenum appears normal.

PELVIS:  Loops of small bowel demonstrate no signs of ileus or obstruction.
The appendix is retrocecal and appears normal. There is bowel wall thickening
involving the ascending and transverse colon and to a lesser extent the
descending colon which is most compatible with an infectious etiology.
Differential a considerations do include an inflammatory or ischemic component
though these are not favored. There is no evidence of pneumatosis, free air or
extraluminal fluid collection. There is a small amount of free fluid in the
pelvis. A few scattered diverticula are noted without evidence of
diverticulitis. The uterus appears normal. No adnexal masses are seen. The
urinary bladder is normal.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: Unremarkable..

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Acute colitis, likely infectious most notable involving the right colon.
No evidence of acute complication.
2.  Probable gastritis.
3.  Cirrhosis with signs of portal hypertension and small volume ascites.
